1.

This is the prosecution of accused persons namely Vipin, Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat Singh pursuant to charge sheet filed by Police Station Sangam Vihar U/s 498A/304B/34 Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) subsequent to the investigation carried out by them in FIR No. 379/18.
2.
As per the case of prosecution, DD no. 43A dated 18.09.2018 regarding suicide committed by a lady at Sangam Vihar was received.

On receipt of the said State vs Vipin Etc on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81009922/
1 information, ASI Ved Prakash along with Ct. Gajanand reached at the spot i.e. H.no.
19/116, K Block, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi where they came to know that lady namely Sandhya has committed suicide by hanging herself and her husband i.e. Vipin (accused) has taken her to hospital.
Vide DD no. 56A information qua admission of Sandhya vide MLC no. 854/18 was given to ASI Ved Prakash.

On preliminary inquiry, it was found that deceased Sandhya was married to Vipin 20-25 days ago so the information regarding the same was communicated to SDM, Kalkaji who recorded the statement of parents of deceased on 19.09.2018 and conducted the proceedings u/s 176 Cr.P.C.
3.
On the complaint of Sh. Bhagwan Singh, father of the deceased, present FIR was registered on 19.09.2018 u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
As per the contents of the complaint, daughter of the complainant/deceased namely Sandhya left her house on 23.08.2018 at about 04.00 PM and did not return home.
On this, complainant filed her missing report at PS Sangam Vihar on 24.08.2018.
On 28.08.2018, the complainant received a call from PS Sangam Vihar where her daughter was present along with accused Vipin and stated that they got married.
Complainant asked her to come with him but she refused and stated that she will live with accused Vipin only.

On 18.09.2018 at about 07.00 PM landlord of the complainant told the complainant that he had received a call from the matrimonial house of Sandhya (deceased) and stated that Sandhya has committed suicide.

On this, complainant reached at PS Sangam Vihar and told them that accused persons namely Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat (mother and Brother of the accused Vipin) had demanded dowry amounting to Rs. 6,00,000/-, 2-3 days prior to the said incident and also stated that if he did not gave the money,
they will not accept her daughter (deceased).
Allegedly, accused persons harassed the deceased for dowry and threatened her to face consequences for not meeting the demand and all these circumstances lead the deceased to commit suicide.

On this complaint, the present FIR was registered u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
4.
The matter was investigated, accused Vipin was arrested and various exhibits were seized.
Forensic opinion was obtained and statement of the witnesses were recorded.

After the conclusion of the investigation carried out in the FIR no. 379/18, police filed the present charge sheet against the accused persons namely Vipin, Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat Singh u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
5.
Vide Order dated 15.11.2018, Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate concerned took cognizance of offences u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC and the accused persons were called upon to face the trial.
All the accused persons were supplied with the charge sheet and other relevant documents in compliance to section 207 Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as Cr.P.C.).
Thereafter, the present matter was received by way of committal to the Court of Sessions on 01.12.2018.
CHARGE 6.

After hearing the arguments of both the sides, vide order dated 01.08.2023, charge for the offence punishable u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC was framed by this Court against the accused persons namely Vipin, Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat Singh who pleaded not guilty and chose to face trial.

ARGUMENTS :
21.
Ld. Additional PP for State has argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the case of prosecution and their testimony has remained unrebutted.

It is argued that a young lady committed suicide within a month of marriage on account of cruelty and harassment caused by the accused persons and the accused persons have failed to rebutt the presumptions of law which proves their guilt.
That on a combined reading of testimony of prosecution witnesses, offence U/s 498A/304B/34 IPC is proved beyond doubt.
Counsel for the accused persons argued that the prosecution has failed to prove on record the guilt of the accused persons as no substantial evidence has been lead on record.

It is argued that the family members of the deceased are the interested witnesses who have deposed falsely without any substance and have failed to prove the essential elements to attract the offences charged against the accused persons.

It is further submitted that the main ingredients for the offences u/s 498A IPC and 304 B IPC have not been fulfilled as the prosecution has failed to prove the cruelty and demand of dowry by the accused persons.

Learned defence counsel contended that the prosecution is obliged to prove the existence of all the essential ingredients of the offence under Section 304B IPC, beyond reasonable doubt and only then the presumption under Section 113 B of the Evidence Act can be raised against the accused.

In the instant case, the prosecution has failed to prove their case, hence,
accused persons are entitled to be acquitted.

In support of his arguments, the defence has relied upon following judgments 1. Dugra Prasad & Anr. v. The State of M.P., Criminal appeal no. 1081 of 2010 (arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 5450 of 2009) passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

FINDINGS:
24. Arguments adduced by Ld.

Additional APP for State, Ld. Counsel for the complainant and Ld.
Defence Counsel for the accused persons have been heard.
Evidences and documents on record perused carefully.

25. Before adverting to the facts of the present case and the rival contentions raised, let the provisions of law be reproduced and the essential ingredient be enumerated that were required to be proved by the prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused persons.

Section 304B of IPC says:
(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection, with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
(2) ........
Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act says:

When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry,
the court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.

Section 498A of IPC says:

6

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation- For the purpose of this section, "Cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman;
or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
26. For proving the offence u/s 498A IPC
, the prosecution was required to establish that woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment either by husband of the woman or by the relative of the husband.

For the purpose of this section, cruelty means that any willful conduct which is of such nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her or where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or is on account of failure by her to make that demand.
Cruelty for the purpose of constituting the offence u/s 498A IPC need not be physical.

Even mental torture in a given case would be case of cruelty within the meaning of section 498A IPC.
27.
The prosecution was required to prove the foundational facts before presumption of law is attracted and the burden of proof is shifted upon the accused.

Presumption under section 113B is a presumption of law that shall be raised only on proof of the following essentials;
(i) The death of a woman must have been caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances.
( ii) Such death must have occurred within seven years of her marriage.
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her relatives.
(iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
(v) The woman is subjected to such cruelty or harassment soon before her death.
28. Now this Court shall proceed on to deal with the five aspects / essentials enumerated above one by one to see whether the prosecution has been able to prove the same.

sentences.text: 29. It is the admitted case that the deceased Sandhya died otherwise than under normal circumstances.

The postmortem report of deceased i.e. Ex. PW8/3 that has been duly proved on record proves that the death of the deceased Sandhya was due to asphyxia due to antemortem hanging and as such it was unnatural and was not under normal circumstances.
This aspect stands duly established.
(ii) Such death must have occurred with in seven years of her marriage.
30. It is not disputed that the accused and the deceased got married on 30.08.2018 and she died on 18.09.2018.
Certificate of marriage is Ex. A3 (Colly), hence, the deceased Sandhya died within a month of her marriage which means within seven years of her marriage, hence, this aspect also stands duly proved.
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her relatives and (iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
31. Both the aforesaid aspects are taken together being inter connected for the purpose of discussion and findings.
There are five material prosecution witnesses on whose testimony the case of prosecution rests.

Three are the family members of deceased i.e. PW1 Bhagwan Singh (father), PW2 Smt. Somvati (mother) and PW3 Sh. Vinod Kumar (brother) and two are the independent public witnesses that are PW4 Ankit Goyal and PW5 Madhu.

It is to be seen from the testimony of these witnesses as to whether they have been able to establish the fact of causing of cruelty/harassment to deceased by accused persons to meet the demand of dowry which driven the deceased to commit suicide.
32. Now coming to the deposition of PW-1 Sh. Bhagwan Singh, father of the deceased, PW2 Somwati, mother of the deceased and PW3 Sh. Vinod Kumar, brother of the deceased.
The testimony of all the three witnesses are verbatim same.

PW1, PW2 and PW3 stated in their examination in chief that on 09.09.2018 accused Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat had come to their house and demanded dowry of Rs. 6,00,000/- and said "yadi dehej ki maang nahi puri hogi to tumhari ladki k saath bahut bura hoga".
They further stated that on one more occasion after 09.09.2018, the aforesaid accused came to their house and again demanded Rs. 6,00,000/- as dowry.

Another incriminating statement made by them is that Sandhya told Vinod that accused Vipin used to beat her on account of non fulfilling of demand of dowry of Rs. 6,00,000/-.
33.

At the outset, it is to be noted that the witnesses PW1 and PW2 nowhere in their examination in chief stated that the accused persons caused any harassment or cruelty in any manner to the deceased Sandhya for meeting the demands of dowry.
It is nowhere stated by them in their examination in chief that accused persons demanded any dowry from the deceased Sandhya during her matrimonial life.

As far as statement of PW1 qua information about the beating of Sandhya by State vs Vipin Etc on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81009922/
8 accused Vipin on account of non fulfilling of demand of dowry of Rs. 6,00,000/-, the said information of PW1 is received by him from his son Vinod which falls in the realm of hearsay evidence that cannot be admitted or considered.

sentences.text: 34. As far as statement of PW3 qua allegation of cruelty is concerned where in his examination in chief he stated that after 09.09.2018 his sister Sandhya had met him on the way and stated him about the harassment caused by accused Vipin, no specific date or time has been mentioned by PW3 when he met his sister.

PW3 has also not specified as to where he was going or from where his sister Sandhya was coming and at which particular point they met whereby the only above single fact has been conveyed to him by her.
PW3 has not stated that Sandhya discussed other issues also or she asked about well being of her parents.

No evidence has been lead on record either by way of call detail records or any independent public witness to show that PW3 and the deceased Sandhya were in talking terms or that they met or exchanged calls during her matrimonial lifetime.
35. Admittedly, no police complaint has been filed by PW1, PW2 and PW3 against the accused persons qua any alleged incident of beating or harassment caused to deceased during her life time.
No MLC was ever prepared to support the allegations of PW1, PW2 and PW3.
It is not disputed that no such incident of beating has happened in the presence of PW1, PW2 or PW3.
Thus, the allegations of cruelty or harassment could not be substantiated by the prosecution witnesses during the evidence.
36. Now coming to the allegations of demand of dowry of Rs. 6,00,000/- made by PW1, PW2 and PW3 against accused Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat.
Firstly, they have not stated the particular time during the day when the accused came to their house for raising such demand.

Secondly, none of the aforesaid witnesses in their previous statement recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. or the one recorded by SDM has mentioned the date when such demand was raised, that renders the above statements of PW1,
PW2 and PW3 as improvised statements which cannot be believed upon or considered.
The other circumstances surrounding that have appeared in the case during the evidence also suggest otherwise negating the claim of PW1, PW2 and PW3 that are discussed in following paragraphs.
37. It is not disputed that accused Vipin and deceased Sandhya entered into a love marriage against the wishes of their respective parents and were residing separately from them.
PW1, PW2 and PW3 in their examination-in-chief stated that deceased Sandhya left the house on 23.08.2018 and a missing report was filed on 24.08.2018.
Thereafter, on 28.08.2018 a call was received from PS Sangam Vihar where Sandhya and accused Vipin were present and the prosecution witnesses were informed that they both had got married.
PW1, PW2 and PW3 further stated that they asked Sandhya to come with them but she refused to do so and said that she will stay with accused Vipin.
It is nowhere claimed by PW1, PW2 and PW3 in their examination in chief that they remained in touch with the deceased Sandhya after 28.08.2018 till her death on 18.09.2018.

There is no call detail records between deceased Sandhya and her family members gathered by the Investigating officer or produced on record to show that between 28.08.2018 till 18.09.2018 they were in touch or they talked to each other.

9 38.

The conduct of PW1 and his family members is also clear from the fact that after having the information of suicide committed by Sandhya at her matrimonial house, they rush to police station instead of visiting the matrimonial house of Sandhya which was hardly at a distance of 100 metre from their house to see her condition which apparently show that PW1 or his family members did not have much concern for Sandhya as she married against their wishes.
39.
PW1 and PW2 could not tell the exact date or month or place of marriage performed between the deceased and accused Vipin.

PW1 and PW2 during cross examination stated that they were not even aware whether Sandhya and Vipin were residing on rent since 01.09.2018 nor they were aware about the place of their rented accommodation till the death of Sandhya which shows that they were least bothered about the matrimonial life of their deceased daughter Sandhya and did not have any contact with them.

40. It is also relevant to note that PW1, PW2 or PW3 have not lodged any complaint against the accused persons with the police or conveyed the fact of demand of dowry raised by the accused persons to Sandhya during her lifetime.

An isolated statement mentioning that the demand was raised on 09.09.2018 without mentioning the time or occasion when such demand was raised that too when PW1, PW2 and PW3 have failed to establish that they had any conversation or relation with the accused or his family members does not make sense or inspire the confidence of the court to believe upon.
41. PW1, PW2 and PW3 alleged that accused Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat while demanding dowry stated that "yadi dehej ki maang nahi puri hogi to tumhari ladki k saath bahut bura hoga".
It is relevant to note that accused Vipin got married with the deceased against wishes of his parents and was residing separately from them which shows that they have not accepted their marriage.
Now if accused Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat did not have accepted their marriage and did not allow Vipin to reside with them

, then no question or ocassion arises for the aforesaid accused persons to approach PW1 or his family members for raising the demand of dowry as a condition to accept the deceased as their daughter-in-law.
In such circumstances, it is highly improbable to believe that accused would ask or expect dowry from PW1 or his family members as alleged herein.
Thus, in view of the discussion above it can be seen that the testimony of PW1, PW2 and PW3 failed to establish the fact of demanding of dowry as alleged by them.
Moreover, in absence of cruelty or harassment that too for meeting the demands of dowry, mere demand of dowry will not be sufficient to attract the provisions of section 304B IPC.
The cruelty or harassment has to be in relation to demand of dowry for invoking the aforesaid provisions.
42. The testimony of PW1, PW2 and PW3 discussed above does not inspire confidence of the court.
Neither the same has been able to establish the cruelty or harassment caused to deceased Sandhya by the accused persons nor the fact that such was done to meet the demand of dowry.

Above all, the demand of dowry by the accused persons also could not be established by the testimony of PW1,
PW2 and PW3 in view of the discrepancies appearing in their testimony as discussed in previous paragraphs.

Both the witnesses have failed to support the case of the prosecution in any manner.
The testimony of PW4 and PW5 did not corroborate the testimony of family members of deceased.
Thus, the testimony of PW4 and PW5 are of no help to the case of the prosecution.
44. The deceased was an independent lady who took a bold step to go against her parents for getting married with accused Vipin and stayed with him.
During her stay in her matrimonial home, she never lodged any complaint regarding harassment on account of dowry demands to the police or any other authority.
She did not even told about the same to her parents which would have been in natural course if she had faced any such hostile environment in her matrimonial house.
No medical evidence emerged to infer if at any time, that deceased was taken to hospital for physical beatings allegedly given to her.
Absence of these material factors go against the case of the prosecution.

Reliance is placed on Naveen v. The State (GNCT of Delhi), 2014 SCC Online Del 4355 where the above factors have been duly considered and given weight that helps in dislodging of burden upon the accused and compel to draw adverse inference against the prosecution.

sentences.text: 45. In judgment State of NCT of Delhi v. Rakesh & or, 2012 SCC Online DEL 2816 it was held that "the onus lay on the prosecution to establish beyond doubt that the deceased was subjected to matrimonial cruelty or harassment for or in connection with the demand of dowry 'soon' before her death".

entities.text: State of NCT of Delhi v. Rakesh & or, 2012 SCC Online DEL 2816
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The testimonies of the material witnesses of the prosecution have been discussed in the previous paragraphs.
In nutshell, this court has reached to a conclusion that testimony of material witnesses are not consistent and are full of embellishments that does not inspire the confidence of the court.
Admittedly, none of the prosecution witness discussed above has given details or particulars such as date, time or occasion when the accused persons allegedly tortured or beaten deceased Sandhya.
The prosecution witnesses could not even establish the fact of demand of dowry made by the accused persons.

Reliance is placed upon Vipin Jaiswal v. State of AP, 2013, STPL, 198 SC where it has been held that "general allegations of harassment without bringing on record any specific acts of cruelty or harassment is not sufficient to discharge the onus on the prosecution.

entities.text: Vipin Jaiswal v. State of AP, 2013, STPL, 198 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 46. In view of the discussion above, and the evidence lead on record, this court thus concludes that the prosecution has failed to establish both the aforesaid essential requirements i.e. neither it has been able to establish the causing of cruelty/harassment to Sandhya by accused persons nor it could establish that any such willful conduct of accused persons was to meet the demand of dowry.
The aforesaid aspects (iii) & (iv) stands answered accordingly.
(v) The woman is subjected to such cruelty or harassment soon before her death.

47. As the essential requirements mentioned at serial no. (iii) and (iv) that the deceased Sandhya was subjected to cruelty or harassment in order to meet the demand of dowry could not be established so question of "soon before her death" does not arise.
This aspect also remained unproved.

48. Ld. Counsel for the complainant has raised the argument that the photographs placed on record exhibited as Ex. FA2 (colly) reflects that the feet of the deceased are touching the ground and she is State vs Vipin Etc on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81009922/
11
not found hanging nor her facial features show that her death has taken place by way of hanging.
It is further argued that the accused has killed Sandhya by strangulation and thereafter tried to hang her with the ceiling fan to portray that she has committed suicide.
Ld. Counsel for the complainant further argued that the offence u/s 302 IPC is made out against the accused persons.
49. At the outset, it is to be noted that the case of prosecution is that of dowry death and not of murder.
The charge sheet itself was filed after concluding the investigation for the offence u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC which otherwise has not been proved as discussed in the preceding paragraphs.
The argument of the complainant is contrary to the case of the prosecution.

Even if the arguments of the complainant are to be considered, mere photographs are not sufficient to prove the commission of offence u/s 302 IPC where all other evidences and circumstances proves the death of Sandhya by way of suicide.

50. In this respect the testimony of PW4 and PW5 is also relevant as per whom, the door was closed from inside where dead body of Sandhya was recovered when her husband accused Vipin was trying to knock the door and finally opened the same.
PW4 and PW5 were cross examined by Ld.

Additional PP for the state in which suggestions were put that PW4 and PW5 had seen the deceased Sandhya hanging in her room with fan when Vipin pushed the door and as a consequence kundi of the door was broken.

Though, the aforesaid witnesses have turned hostile but again as per the case of prosecution the fact that the dead body of Sandhya was hanging inside the room and the door was closed from inside which was forcefully opened by the accused Vipin remains.

51. Further, the cause of death of Sandhya is proved from the post mortem report which says that it is asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging and it does not say that she was strangulated and the same has been established on record by the testimony of PW8 Dr. Jay Narayan Pandit.

The post mortem report PW8/3 and the circumstances discussed above contradicts the argument of Ld.
Counsel for the complainant.
Thus, nothing on record suggests or proves the ingredients of Section 302 IPC as argued by the Ld. Counsel for the complainant.
52. Ld. Counsel for the complainant has argued that the burden was upon the accused persons to prove the circumstances under which Sandhya died which they failed to explain.
This court do not find much substance in the contention of the Ld. Counsel for the complainant.

Accused in their statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. has explained the circumstances that the deceased was under pressure, emotionally disturbed as her family was not supporting her in her marriage with the accused Vipin due to caste difference.
It is further stated that Sandhya was constantly called upon to leave her husband which probably triggered the emotionally disturbed Sandhya to loose her control and commit suicide.

Though the accused persons have not stepped into the witness box to substantiate their plea of defence by examining themselves but in the given scenario of society prevailing in this country the inter caste marriage is not accepted in many segments of society even today, hence, the plea of accused is acceptable.
The families even go to the extent of honour killing in some cases and considered it to be a stigma on their status.

The circumstances which accused have been able to show by cross examination of PW1,

12 PW2 and PW3 some how probablises their plea of defence.

53. In judgment titled as "Narender Singh Arora v. State of NCT of Delhi and others, 2010 SCC online DEL 2980" it is observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that:-
"Suicide is a known phenomenon of human nature.

entities.text: Narender Singh Arora v. State of NCT of Delhi and others, 2010 SCC online DEL 2980
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Suicides are committed by living human beings for various reasons, some are not able to bear the normal stresses which are common in life.
Some are not able to cope up with the circumstances in which they are placed.
Some commit suicide because of frustration of not achieving the desired goals.
There are many cases where students commit suicide because they failed to achieve certain percentage of marks.
Some commit suicide because they are not able to retain top position, some commit suicide because they are not able to cope with the demands of life.
Some commit suicide because they suffer sudden loss, some commit suicide out of fear of being caught.
There are various reasons for which suicides are committed by men and women.
All suicides are unnatural deaths.
Suicide is a complex phenomenon.
One, who commits suicide, is not alive to disclose as to what was going on in his or her mind when he or she committed suicide.

There is no presumption that every suicide committed by a married woman in her in-laws'
house or at her parents' house has to be because she was suffering harassment at the hands of her husband or her in- laws".
54.

As it has been observed in the aforesaid judgment, that there is no presumption that every suicide committed by a married woman in her in-laws' house or at her parents' house has to be because she was suffering harassment at the hands of her husband or her in- law.
Suicides are committed by living human beings for various reasons, some are not able to bear the normal stresses which are common in life.
Some are not able to cope up with the circumstances in which they are placed.
Some commit suicide because of frustration of not achieving the desired goals.

Here in the instant case also the prosecution has miserably failed to prove on record that deceased was harassed by accused during her life time that might have drove her to commit suicide rather the circumstances appearing on record indicates otherwise and probablises the plea of defence taken by the accused.
55. In Baijnath and ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2017) 1 Supreme Court Cases 101 it was observed that Section 113B of the Act enjoins a statutory presumption as to dowry death.

entities.text: Baijnath and ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2017) 1 Supreme Court Cases 101
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Noticeably this presumption as well is founded on the proof of cruelty or harassment of the woman dead for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the person charged with the offence.

The presumption as to dowry death thus would get activated only upon the proof of the fact that the deceased lady had been activated only upon the proof of the fact that the deceased lady had been subjected to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the accused and that too in the reasonable contiguity of death.

A conjoint reading of these three provisions, thus predicates the burden of the prosecution to unassailably substantiate the ingredients of the two offences by direct and convincing evidence so as to avail the presumption engrafted in section 113B of the Act against the accused.

Proof of cruelty or State vs Vipin Etc on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81009922/
13
harassment by the husband or her relative or the person charged is thus the sine qua non to inspirit the statutory presumption, to draw the person charged within the coils thereof.

If the prosecution fails to demonstrate by cogent, coherent and persuasive evidence to prove such fact, the person accused of either of the above referred offences cannot be held guilty by taking refuge only of the presumption to cover up the shortfall in proof.

56. As the essential elements discussed in the preceding paragraphs have not been complied, it can be safely conducted that prosecution has failed to prove even foundational facts so presumption of law does not get attracted and the onus remained on the shoulders of the prosecution only.

57. Patently, cruelty or harassment of the lady by her husband or his relative for or in connection with any demand for any property or valuable security as a demand for dowry or in connection therewith is the common constituent of both the offences that is u/s 498A and 304B of IPC.
A cumulative consideration of the overall evidence on the facet of dowry, leaves this court unconvinced about the truthfulness of the charge qua the accused persons.
The prosecution has failed to prove this indispensable component of the two offences beyond reasonable doubt.

The factum of unnatural death in the matrimonial home and that too within seven years of marriage therefore is thus ipso facto not sufficient to bring home the charge under sections 304B and 498A of the code against them.
CONCLUSION 58.
It is a settled proposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case on judicial file beyond reasonable doubt by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence.
The burden of proof of the version of the prosecution in a criminal trial throughout the trial is on the prosecution.

Also, it is a settled proposition of criminal law that accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt if any in the prosecution story and such reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal.
59.

In view of the material inconsistencies in the testimony of the prosecution witnesses and due to lack of cogent evidence lead on record, this Court is of the view that prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The evidence coming on record entitles the accused persons for the benefit of doubt.
Therefore, the accused persons namely Vipin, Nirmala @ Parwati and Rajat Singh are hereby acquitted of the charges levelled against them in the present case.
